title: Introduce subnet reconciliation worker and endpoint route prioritizer
author: Maya Singh
description: Background: Multiple customers and internal upgrades surfaced two classes of flakes in private control plane installs: (1) transient drift between Terraform state and actual subnet ownership/tagging after mass-tenant migrations which caused endpoint provisioning to pick the wrong AZ and (2) race conditions during control-plane HA failover where multiple route entries to the same interface endpoint ended up with ambiguous precedence. This PR introduces an idempotent reconciliation worker plus route-priority metadata so the installer can operate safely during large-scale upgrades. Changes include: a) a small long-running controller (go) that can be enabled via Helm values to reconcile 'redwood:owner' subnet tags and re-run Terraform apply only when ownership drift is detected; b) Terraform module change to surface routePriority and routeWeight on aws_route and to generate route entries with deterministic naming to avoid accidental duplicates on reapply; c) installer hook in Helm (pre-upgrade/post-upgrade) that snapshots current endpoint route table state and records a compact restore manifest to allow fast rollback of route entries; d) security hardening for endpoint SGs to avoid overly-broad egress rules created by older installer runs; e) unit + integration tests (local aws-sim) and an e2e smoke test added to perf-canary harness. Motivation: reduce incident surface during multi-AZ capacity handoffs and make upgrades and rollbacks deterministic and auditable. Checklist: - [x] implement reconciliation worker with exponential backoff and leader election - [x] add routePriority/routeWeight support in terraform modules - [x] add Helm hooks + snapshot/restore utility - [x] add tests (unit, integration, e2e smoke) - [x] update docs/upgrade-notes and release notes - [x] telemetry: add metric redwood_private.subnet_reconcile.count and route_rewrites.count How it works (high level): The reconcile worker periodically lists subnets and validates the 'redwood:owner' tag and an ownership annotation stored in a Terraform-managed SSM parameter. If mismatch is found the worker queues a reconciliation job which either patches tags (when safe) or triggers an idempotent terraform plan/apply with a short TTL lock to avoid concurrent applies. For endpoint routing we now write a small metadata JSON into a dedicated S3 bucket (installer-state) that contains routePriority and last-modified; the installer prefers higher-priority routes during failover and removes duplicates during cleanup. Rollback: Helm hook snapshot contains the exact prefixed route ids and SG entries to reapply; the installer restore utility is idempotent. Backwards compatibility: when routePriority is absent, the code falls back to hashed deterministic ordering based on subnet creation time. Risk & mitigation: terraform apply can be noisy; we gate automatic applies behind a feature flag and only enable automatic reapply when the admin opt-in value is set. Tests: ran full integration in staging, smoke e2e passed. See files changed for details.

release_notes: installer: add optional subnet reconciliation worker and route priority metadata for endpoint routing; Helm hooks to snapshot endpoint routes during upgrades; Terraform modules expose routePriority. Opt-in automatic applies behind helm.installer.reconcile.autoApply flag. Includes security tightening for endpoint SGs and rollback helpers.
rollback_instructions: Use the helm pre-upgrade snapshot stored as a ReleaseHook artifact (installer-route-snapshot-<release>.json) and run pkg/installer/restore/restore --snapshot path --dry-run to validate; to revert code changes, roll back Helm chart to previous chart version and run restore utility. Automatic terraform reapply is disabled by default; if enabled, disable helm.installer.reconcile.autoApply before rollback.
security_implications: Tightens endpoint security groups by default and adds a remediation script for clusters with overly-broad egress rules. The reconcile worker requires IAM permissions limited to Describe/Tag subnets, Get/Put SSM parameter, and conditionally ExecuteChangeSet/Apply when autoApply is enabled. Recommended to scope the role tightly and enable auditor logs.
notes_for_ops: Operator knobs: helm.installer.reconcile.enabled (bool), helm.installer.reconcile.autoApply (bool), helm.installer.route.priorityBucketCount (int). Monitoring: redwood_private.subnet_reconcile.count, redwood_private.route_rewrites.count, redwood_private.reconcile_errors.rate. If reconcile_jobs spike, temporarily disable autoApply and run manual remediation.
